newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Nestle says China reforms irreversible.
newsitem.headline: Nestle says China reforms irreversible.

text.p: Global food and beverages group Nestle SA said it saw no reason for business conditions in China to worsen after the death of economic reform leader Deng Xiaoping.
"In my view, the process of liberalisation is irreversible," said Michael Garrett, Nestle executive vice-president responsible for Asia, Oceania and Africa.
Garrett told Reuters he expected no fundamental changes as China's economic policy had shown continuity for a number of years.
"I am therefore confident that the death of Deng Xiaoping will not affect Nestle's presence and business prospects in China," Garrett said.
Nestle chairman Helmut Maucher last October said he expected its initial investment in China of 2.8 billion yuan to grow to five billion yuan by 2000 and sales to double every two years.

Nestle has local plants in China producing its core portfolio of milk products, instant coffee, chocolate, confectionary and prepared foods, with a new plant for mineral water scheduled to open this year.
